facts.fact: The health ministry's national health development plan 2024-2028, adopted in Council of Ministers on 23 February 2024, sets as a result to develop and deploy by end December 2028 a DHIS2 platform integrating all health programmes, with training of data managers at the three levels of the health pyramid, user guides and six-monthly data validation sessions; its axis 5 on the national health information system is costed at 3,509,631,187 FCFA, 0.68% of the plan's 514.3 billion.

The plan adopted on 23 February 2024 names the ministry's 'Projet SNIS' as responsible for implementing the DHIS2 platform, with WHO as partner, and sets the ministry the tasks of adopting the legal framework of the SNIS and making its management bodies (health observatory, statistics directorate) functional by 2028.

note: Passages file only. The SNIS is classed hmis as the routine reporting system the DHIS2 platform is planned to carry; the plan describes a deployment still to come, so no tiers, digitised or clinics fact is taken. Its situation analysis (plan text dated November 2023) calls the SNIS globally dysfunctional, with transmission deadlines not met, little or no data processing at department and region, low availability of ICT, a change-management strategy for use of the computer tool written but not applied, and much private-sector data escaping it; none of this states where data is keyed. The 'nouveau SIS' for 6 CHU, 8 CHR and 30 health centres is not described in the passages and is left unclassified; if the parent reads it as the eGabon-SIS emr, the plan is a current plan naming it. The plan also provides for community health indicators to enter the SNIS tools (7.1.8). An earlier SNIS master plan (SDSSIS 2017-2022) is named, with a 2024-2029 successor to be written.
